expectations.text: Names at least one fintech benchmark (Stripe, Mercury, Ramp, or Wise) together with a specific borrowed mechanic, not just the product name
expectations.evidence: No industry benchmark named anywhere. Design direction is given as raw hex values and font choices with no product reference or borrowed mechanic.

expectations.text: The generated prompt's content inventory preserves all four currently rendered data points (date, description, amount, status)
expectations.evidence: DATA block covers date, description, amount_cents+currency, status — all four rendered fields preserved.

expectations.text: Identifies data already in the API response but not rendered today (currency, counterparty, payment_method, or has_more pagination)
expectations.evidence: Uses counterparty and payment_method in the prompt but never identifies them as currently-unrendered free wins, and turns has_more into an invented cursor-paginated 'Load more' feature rather than flagging it.

expectations.text: The prompt block is self-contained — it does not reference file paths, the codebase, or other sections of the document a design tool cannot see
expectations.evidence: The fenced block is self-contained — audience, data, states, visual direction and an ASCII wireframe, with no reference to the codebase.

expectations.text: Proposes at least one additive API change with a method and path (or an optional field on the existing endpoint) plus a response shape, explicitly marked non-breaking
expectations.evidence: No API section at all. No endpoint, shape, or non-breaking note proposed, despite the prompt introducing pagination and filter controls that need backing data.

expectations.text: Does not propose removing, renaming, or changing the type of any existing field in GET /api/transactions
expectations.evidence: No existing field in GET /api/transactions is removed, renamed, or retyped.
